slides.1.title: Level 3 recap
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Viticulture and climate
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Côte-Rôtie: hand harvest, ≥6,000 vines/ha; southern old-vine Grenache, Mistral, frost and hail; climate direction: earlier, more alcohol, less acid; VIFA: ≤5% of area, ≤10% of blend, 10-year trial
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Winemaking and style
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Viognier co-fermented with Syrah (≤20% of vines); Grenache oxidises easily and is complemented by Syrah/Mourvèdre; VDN fortified at 5–10%; vin de paille dried ≥45 days; ancestrale a single fermentation in bottle
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Comparison and rules
slides.1.highlights.2.content: A Rhône cru = an independent AOC while Burgundy ranks within villages; proportions are on estate plantings; Vin de France has no geographical indication but may show variety and vintage; a cru label omits 'Villages'
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Industry and essays
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Inter Rhône is the interprofession; bulk about 64% of 2024/25 despatches; top export markets by volume: Belgium, UK, USA (2025); Laudun is the 18th cru in 2024; essay = position + evidence + counter-argument + conclusion
slides.1.content: Completing the assessment finishes Level 3; confirm the exam format against the latest official specifications.

What are Côte-Rôtie's harvest and density rules?
A. Hand harvest, at least 6,000 vines per hectare
B. Machine harvest, 3,000 vines per hectare
C. Any harvest method, no density rule
Hand harvest, at least 6,000 vines per hectare.
What are the VIFA limits on estate area and blend in Côtes du Rhône?
Area ≤5%, blend ≤10%, with a 10-year observation period.
Which is the only red variety among the VIFA trial varieties?
Vidoc is red; the other three are white.
What is the main direction of climate impact on southern Rhône Grenache?
A. Earlier harvest, higher potential alcohol, lower acidity
The direction is earlier, more sugar, less acid (specific figures are indicative).
What is the Côte-Rôtie rule on Viognier and Syrah?
A. Viognier may be up to 20% of vines in Syrah plots, vinified together from blended grapes
D. Viognier must be fermented separately and added
Syrah ≥80%, Viognier at most 20% of vines, vinified together.
In a VDN such as Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise, neutral spirit is added at what share of the must volume?
5–10%, stopping fermentation and keeping natural sugar.
Why is Grenache often blended with Syrah and Mourvèdre?
A. Grenache is low in colour and tannin and oxidises easily, so colour and structure are added
B. Grenache is too high in acid
This is the classic reason for blending Grenache (general account).
What is the key difference between Rhône cru and Burgundy classification?
A. Burgundy ranks plots within a village (Premier / Grand Cru) while a Rhône cru is an independent AOC with no ranked subdivisions
C. The Rhône ranks by plot
One Rhône cru = one AOC; Burgundy ranks by plot (climat).
A label reading 'Gigondas' (not 'Côtes du Rhône Villages Gigondas') indicates?
B. Villages with an added name
D. An independent cru (its own AOC)
A cru is an independent AOC and uses its own name on the label.
A Vin de France label may?
A. Carry no geographical indication but may show variety and vintage
Under EU rules variety and vintage may be shown, but no geographical name.
